subject: Outbound control acceptance and evidence for private endpoint
messages:
From: A. Ramos <andrea.ramos@edgehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Outbound IP and firewall expectations for private endpoint

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our security team asked for a concise acceptance checklist we can use to validate the private endpoint rollout in our VPC. Specifically they want to confirm:

- Definitive outbound IPs (or deterministic ranges) for Redwood control-plane callbacks and model fetches.
- Firewall rules required on our side (ports, destination FQDNs/IPs, and recommended protocols).
- Any short-lived/burst addresses or CDN-backed endpoints we should not rely on for permanent allowlisting.
- Logging/audit evidence that Redwood can provide for a compliance handoff.

Can you produce something we can hand to infrastructure for allowlist approval? If you can attach a one-page evidence CSV or a sample rule set, that would help our change window.

Appreciate it — Andrea
NOC, EdgeHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Andrea Ramos <andrea.ramos@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound IP and firewall expectations for private endpoint

Andrea —

Thanks for the clear list. I put together an opinionated acceptance artifact and a short implementation checklist for your infra team. High-level notes up-front:

1) Deterministic egress: For Redwood Private we provide a small set of static egress IPs (attached CSV) that are stable for the "Dedicated controlplane" lane. If you are using our on-prem connector mode with NAT behind customer-owned NAT, provide those egress IPs to your firewall team for permanent allowlisting.

2) Ports and protocols: TCP 443 outbound to our controlplane endpoints is the only required flow for model control API and health checks. If you enable metric ingestion we will request 443 to our ingestion endpoint as well. No inbound ports required.

3) CDN / ephemeral endpoints: We DO use short-lived hostnames for some model-layer distribution (CDN-backed). These should NOT be used for long-term allowlisting. The CSV labels static vs ephemeral for each record.

4) Evidence & logs: We can provide a daily mapping csv with observed egress IPs and a signed manifest (example attached). For audit we can export connection logs (TLS SNI, dest IP, timestamp) for the requested window.

I've attached: egress-ip-evidence.csv (static vs ephemeral, announced time window), and a 1-page firewall-rules-v1.pdf sample rule set your team can drop into change.

Action items:
- Laura: can you add the SLA note about IP rotation notice period (72h) and confirm retention window for exported connection logs?
- Vanessa: confirm whether we need a DocuSign / attestation for their SOC2 intake or a simple signed CSV will be sufficient.
- Andrea: once you have the change window, share the schedule and we will provide a two-day smoke window with ops on-call.

Karthik
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Andrea Ramos <andrea.ramos@edgehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-08T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound IP and firewall expectations for private endpoint

Andrea — quick clarifications from compliance side: we generally provide the following artifacts for allowlist acceptance and audit handoff: 

- Signed egress manifest (CSV) listing static controlplane IPs and the first-observed timestamp; we notify customers at least 72 hours before any planned permanent IP change.
- A one-time export of TLS connection metadata for the requested window (no payload) for your auditors. Retention: we keep detailed connection logs for 30 days by default; extended retention is an add-on.
- Confirmation of ports (TCP 443) and destination hostnames used by the controlplane. Model distribution endpoints are marked as ephemeral in the CSV.
- Recommended firewall rules (sample):
  * Allow outbound TCP 443 to: 54.88.101.12, 54.88.101.13, 3.21.45.90 (controlplane pool) — description: controlplane API and heartbeats.
  * Allow outbound TCP 443 to: 52.211.7.20 (metrics.ingest.redwood.com) — only if metrics are enabled.
  * Deny inbound from those IPs (no inbound requirement).

Please treat the numeric IPs above as examples — use the attached CSV for authoritative values.

Andrea: to accelerate sign-off, can you confirm whether EdgeHealth requires
1) a signed CSV (boolean)
2) a PDF attestation (boolean)
3) longer retention for logs (boolean + desired window)

We will prepare whichever combination you need.

Laura Bennett
Head, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Andrea Ramos <andrea.ramos@edgehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound IP and firewall expectations for private endpoint

Thanks — this is exactly what our change board needs. Quick responses:

1) Signed CSV: yes, required for ticket attachment.
2) PDF attestation: optional but preferred (we'll include as supplemental evidence).
3) Longer retention: we need 90 days for the initial onboarding period, after which we'll revisit.

Attached I'll upload the change ticket once I have the signed CSV. Proposed change window: 2027-06-18 02:00-04:00 UTC. Can your ops on-call cover the smoke tests then?

Andrea
NOC, EdgeHealth
